patch_description: After the refine/growth loop converges, the lattice-based layout still leaves interior voids and under-used boundary regions. Grid-sample the square to find the point maximizing distance to all circle boundaries and the walls (the largest inscribed void radius). If this void radius exceeds ~0.05, insert a new circle there, re-run refine_layout on 27 centers so everything re-equilibrates around the newcomer, and then drop the smallest circle to return to n=26. This is the interior-space generalization of greedy boundary capture: the new circle captures space that the fixed-lattice arrangement cannot, and re-refinement lets neighboring circles redistribute. Repeat the insertion while the sum keeps improving and the void radius stays above the threshold.
